base: origin/main f3b19008 (API 1.9.116, the version production serves)
rule: Written and committed before any code change on lane/r1104-repo-canonical and before any replay. Queries are product names and phrasings a builder types; each expected repo comes from the issue's evidence and the repo's own GitHub page (github.com/theahaco/scaffold-stellar answers HTTP 301 to github.com/stellar-scaffold/cli and the GitHub API names it stellar-scaffold/cli, read 2026-11-04), never from replay output. The 2026-10-23 sets (../2026-10-23-repos-ranking: dev set, battery, exact names, project names, keyword) are replayed beside these, unchanged.
replay: One corpus capture from the public /api/repos read; base and branch searchRepos replayed over it with ../2026-10-23-repos-ranking/replay.mts. Fidelity first: the base replay's first page must match live on at least 90% of captured queries, or the harness is fixed before any result is read.

bars.acceptance: every acceptance query ranks its expected repo first on the branch
bars.controls: every control ranks its expected repo first on base and on the branch
bars.unchanged: every unchanged query serves the same first page (fullName and score, in order), matchMode and total on base and branch
bars.naturalLanguage: reported only, no bar: longer questions that name the same products
bars.existingSets: every rank move in the 2026-10-23 sets is listed; an expected repo that moves down needs a stated reason, or the change fails
bars.generalRule: a general authority rule (first-party ownership or repoScore above the keyword score) is measured as a variant on the same sets; it joins the branch only if it ranks first an acceptance query the curated entries leave unranked and moves no expected repo down in any set
bars.exactName: every exactName query ranks first the repo whose name (the part after the owner) is the query, on the branch; a canonical float never takes rank 1 from an exact name

amended.why: An independent review of the first three commits found inputs the set did not hold: a longer phrase that contains a product name fired the float, an underscore spelling did not, and an exact repo name lost rank 1 to the float. Added before any code change for those findings; no entry above was edited.
